Technology stocks were edging lower Friday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing slightly less than 0.1% in value today while the Philadelphia semiconductor index was posting a more than 0.5% decline.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
- Red Hat ( RHT ) tumbled Friday, sinking as much as 15%, after the open-source software seller issued forecasts for Q2 trailing analyst projections, prompting at least four brokerages to lower their price targets for the company's stock. RBC Capital Markets trimmed its price target by $3 to $177 a share, also maintaining its Outperform rating, while BMO Capital Markets lowered its price target by $15 to $177 a share and reiterated its Market Perform investment recommendation. Also, Monness Crespi & Hardt cut its price target by $14 to $186 a share and Barclays dropped its price by $26 to $160 a share while keeping their Buy and Overweight ratings, respectively. The weaker-than-expected guidance upstaged above-consensus Q1 results, with Red Hat earning $0.72 per share, excluding one-time items, on $813.5 million in revenue. Analysts, on average, had been looking for adjusted Q1 net income of $0.68 per share on $807.5 million in revenue.
In other sector news:
+ Qualcomm ( QCOM ) was rising Friday, turning around a small, mid-morning decline, after the specialty chipmaker extended its cash tender offer for all outstanding shares of NXP Semiconductors ( NXPI ) by another week to June 29. Separately, Qualcomm reportedly is one of seven cornerstone investors who provided China's Xiaomi Corp. with $548 million in new funding ahead of a planned $6.1 billion initial public offering on the Hong Kong stock exchange. Other pre-IPO investors include China Mobile ( CHL ), according to Reuters, which was provided with a term sheet for the deal.
- Twitter ( TWTR ) was trimming a portion of its prior declines, roughly halving a nearly 2% slide previously on Friday, after saying it purchased privately held Smyte to help reduce hateful content on the micro-blogging website. Twitter announced the deal on its @TwitterSafety post, saying the San Francisco-based technology company specializes in safety, spam and security issues and will help it address those issues "more quickly and effectively." Financial terms and other details of the acquisition were not disclosed.
- BlackBerry Limited (BB,BB.TO) retreated Friday, at one point dropping over 10%, after the smartphone manufacturer swung to a GAAP Q1 net loss of $0.11 per share, reversing a $1.23 per share GAAP profit during the year-ago period. Adjusted revenue also fell year-over-year, dropping to $217 million during the three months ended May 31 from $244 million last year but still beating the $209.6 million Street view, while reported revenue fell to $213 million from $235 million during the same quarter last year. Excluding one-time items, Blackberry earned $0.03 per share, improving on a $0.02 per share in net income during the year-ago period and topping the analyst consensus expecting $0.00 per share.
